## Interpretation

**Headline.** The prefix/bare mirror image — the two arms failing on complementary context populations — survives re-reading the same predictions and targets in SAE feature space. The plan's primary statistic, the difference pattern M_c = Δ_prefix − Δ_bare, correlates 0.855 across spaces over the 22 contrasts (perm p < 1e-4, 0/10,000), with 18/20 sign agreement on the dense-significant union, and the same conclusion holds at the individual-context grain: across 9,941 held-out conversations the per-context prefix−bare error difference correlates 0.710 across spaces. The scoped claim is that the mirror **survives this SAE re-basis** — one sparse over-complete basis, the same conversations, the same judged labels, the same banked fits — not that it is coordinate-system-independent in general. That said, the agreement is not a bookkeeping triviality: per-context cross-space coupling per arm is only 0.66–0.75 (an upper bound on shared signal, since shared per-context difficulty inflates it), so the two spaces disagree substantially about individual contexts while agreeing about which categories each arm finds hard.

**Where the (modest) attenuation enters.** The dense-input→SAE-target comparator cells localize it: keeping dense inputs and moving only the read-out space to SAE features leaves the pattern almost intact (ρ_M = 0.946, SA 19/20), while additionally SAE-encoding the input side gives the headline 0.855. So the SAE target basis is essentially pattern-preserving, and what attenuation exists comes from the input encoding — and even that stays deep in Reproduced territory. Pooling conventions do not matter for M (max 0.914, active-fraction 0.837).

**Honest weak spots.** (1) The prefix arm's own 22-contrast profile is the weakest transfer (ρ = 0.412, perm p = 0.0556 — not below 0.05; 10/13 sign agreement); the strong per-arm transfers are bare (0.797) and context (0.759). The mirror-image OBJECT — the difference pattern — is what reproduces strongly, partly because differencing cancels arm-shared level shifts that reshuffle small per-arm deltas. (2) The context arm's category structure thins in SAE space (11 vs 16 BH-significant contrasts) and its max-pooled per-arm pattern does not transfer (ρ = 0.173, p = 0.438) — the dense round already flagged the context arm's weak category structure, and SAE space weakens it further. (3) Both union sign flips (English, translation) are contrasts where M is near zero in at least one space; for English each arm's own delta keeps its dense sign and the flip is a bare-arm magnitude change.

**Dependence and multiplicity.** The 22 category masks overlap (a context belongs to several contrasts), so the contrast-level permutation p and the SA_M binomial threshold are mildly anti-conservative. The converging read that does not share this problem is the per-context difference-pattern correlation over n = 9,941 (0.710, p ≈ 0): it uses each context once and reproduces the same conclusion, which is why I weight it as the primary corroboration rather than leaning on the 22-point statistic alone.

**Floor-adjusted read (robustness only).** Net of the approximate answer-sampling floors, the cross-space pattern correlations stay 0.81–0.94 (19 shared contrasts, all p < 1e-4), and the refusal categories collapse exactly as in the dense round — bare `answer_is_refusal` flips from significantly harder to significantly easier net of floor. This repeats the dense conclusion that refusal-category "difficulty" is largely answer-sampling variance rather than map failure, now in SAE space — but the SAE floors are an approximate construct (SAE encoding of the mean state, K = 4 draws, covering 1,988 of 9,941 contexts), so this stays a robustness read and the verdict stands on the unadjusted battery, per the plan §3 rule.

**What this settles.** The task body asked whether the SAE bare-query cell's earlier feature-level read (bare ≈ degraded context arm) or the dense context-level mirror generalizes. Answer: over CONTEXTS — the object the mirror claim is about — the mirror reproduces in SAE space in full, so the complementarity is a property of the information available to each arm (history vs final query), carried into whichever of the two reading bases we use, rather than an artifact of the dense residual-stream coordinates. This is a same-sample re-basis invariance, not an independent replication: new conversations, a different SAE, or a different layer would be the independence tests.

## Interpretation

**Headline.** The prefix/bare mirror image — the two arms failing on complementary context populations — survives re-reading the same predictions and targets in SAE feature space. The plan's primary statistic, the difference pattern M_c = Δ_prefix − Δ_bare, correlates 0.855 across spaces over the 22 contrasts (perm p < 1e-4, 0/10,000), with 18/20 sign agreement on the dense-significant union, and the same conclusion holds at the individual-context grain: across 9,941 held-out conversations the per-context prefix−bare error difference correlates 0.710 across spaces. The scoped claim is that the mirror **survives this SAE re-basis** — one sparse over-complete basis, the same conversations, the same judged labels, the same banked fits — not that it is coordinate-system-independent in general. That said, the agreement is not a bookkeeping triviality: per-context cross-space coupling per arm is only 0.66–0.75 (an upper bound on shared signal, since shared per-context difficulty inflates it), so the two spaces disagree substantially about individual contexts while agreeing about which categories each arm finds hard.

**Where the (modest) attenuation enters.** The dense-input→SAE-target comparator cells localize it: keeping dense inputs and moving only the read-out space to SAE features leaves the pattern almost intact (ρ_M = 0.946, SA 19/20), while additionally SAE-encoding the input side gives the headline 0.855. So the SAE target basis is essentially pattern-preserving, and what attenuation exists comes from the input encoding — and even that stays deep in Reproduced territory. Pooling conventions do not matter for M (max 0.914, active-fraction 0.837).

**Honest weak spots.** (1) The prefix arm's own 22-contrast profile is the weakest transfer in the verdict space (ρ = 0.412, perm p = 0.0556 — not below 0.05; 10/13 sign agreement); the strong per-arm transfers are bare (0.797) and context (0.759). This weakness is specific to the mean-pooled reading, though: the same prefix read transfers at 0.796 (p = 0.0001) under active-fraction pooling and 0.575 (p = 0.0053) in the dense-input comparator — the verdict space's 0.412 is its floor across variants — while max-pooling instead weakens ALL three per-arm transfers (bare drops to 0.462, p = 0.031) even as ρ_M holds 0.84–0.95. So per-arm profiles are pooling-fragile in both directions where M is not; the mirror-image OBJECT — the difference pattern — is what reproduces strongly, partly because differencing cancels arm-shared level shifts that reshuffle small per-arm deltas. (2) The context arm's category structure thins in SAE space (11 vs 16 BH-significant contrasts) and its max-pooled per-arm pattern does not transfer (ρ = 0.173, p = 0.438) — the dense round already flagged the context arm's weak category structure, and SAE space weakens it further.
